purpose: Sonidegib is used to treat a type of skin cancer called basal cell carcinoma that has come back after surgery or radiation, or that cannot be removed with surgery. It is a targeted therapy, meaning it goes after specific signals that help cancer cells grow. Your doctor prescribed it because your cancer has features that make it respond to this type of treatment.
how_it_works: Inside your body, there is a set of signals called the Hedgehog pathway that helps cells grow normally. In some skin cancers, this pathway gets stuck in the 'on' position, causing cancer cells to keep growing out of control. Sonidegib blocks a key protein in this pathway called Smoothened (SMO), which helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from growing.
common_side_effects: Muscle spasms or cramps, muscle pain or weakness, nausea, diarrhea, tiredness, hair loss or thinning, decreased appetite, taste changes, stomach pain, vomiting, weight loss, and elevated muscle enzymes seen on blood tests.
warnings: This medication can cause serious muscle damage (called rhabdomyolysis), so tell your doctor right away if you have severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine. It can cause serious birth defects and must NEVER be used during pregnancy — use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 20 months after your last dose if you are a woman, or 8 months if you are a man. Do not donate blood during treatment or for 20 months afterward. Avoid grapefruit and St. John's Wort as they can affect how the medication works.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 200 mg (one capsule) taken by mouth once a day on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the capsule whole and do not crush or chew it.
